amajja:
1amajja

anusikkhati:
1anusikkhati
pr. 3 sg. [BHS anuśikṣati], learns, practises, studies; esp. practises (something, acc.) in imitation of (somebody, gen.), folows someone’s example in; follows, imitates (someone, usually gen., occasionally acc.); M I 14,.3 (kittavatā nu kho … satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekam nānusikkhanti kittavatā … vivekaṃ ~anti); S I 52,13* (yuñjaṃ Gotama-sāsane appamattānusikkhare; Spk I 110,.3 : ~are ti sikkhanti); A IV 282,.13 (saddhāsampannānaṃ saddhāsampadaṃ ~ati); Sn 934 (tassa bhagavato … ~e); Ja III 315,14* (tesāhaṃ ~āmi); Ap 211,.20 (mantaṃ ca ~āmi); Mil 61,.27 (ye pi tassa ~anti te pi … nirayaṃ uppajjanti); — part.pr. (a) anusikkha(t), mfn., M II 262,.5 (idha-m-~ato); (b) anusikkhanta, mfn., Sn 294 (tassa vattam ~antā); Th 963 (~antā); Ja I 89,.12 (me savakā pi mamaṃ yeva ~antā piṇḍacāriyavattaṃ pūressantī ti); II 98,.13 (tassa ~anto); Cp 3:5:5 (so pi maṃ ~anto pabbajjaṃ samarocayi); (c) anusikkhamāna, mfn., Vin II 201,.19 (mahānāgānaṃ ~amānā taruṇakā bhiṅkacchāpā); Vism 19,.21 (yassa vā pana ~amāno saddhāya vaḍḍhati); Sp 603,.23; — absol. anusikkhitvā, Mil 353,.14 (-kiriyaṃ ~itvā); — fpp anusikkhitabba, mfn., Sp 3,12* (vaṇṇanā pi sakkacca tasmā ~itabbā); — caus. absol. anusikkhāpetvā, teaching, having taught; Mil 352,.28.

2anusikkhati
3 sg. [probably of fut. of anusāsati; cf anuśākṣyati, BHSG § 31:25], will teach; Ja V 345,7* (ehi taṃ ~āmi; 345,15´ : ~āmī ti anusāsāmi) ≠ 346,25* ≠ VI 62,9* ≠ 84,13* (84,19´ : ~āmī ti sikkhāpemi anusāsāmi).
ceṭaka:
1ceṭaka

[ts], a servant; a slave; Abh 514 (dāso ca ~o pesso); Vin IV 66,.21 (kiṃ pana tvaṃ gahapati mahānāge tiṭṭhamāne ~e nimantesī ti, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se cetake); Ja III 281,.2 (rājā ~e kasā gāhāpetvā ubhosu passesu paharāpesi, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se coraghātake); IV 82,.16 (rājā gaṇhatha dasa bhātike ~e ti uṭṭhahi, Be so; Se cetake ti; Ce, Ee bhātikaceṭake ti); VI 135,18´ (sabbe amhe matthake cūḷaṃ ṭhapetvā attano ~e karohi); Ap 317,.9 (bhatakā ~ā c’ eva, Be, Ce so; Ee gītakā; Se celakā); Cp 2:4:7 (tassā sārattagadhito gāhāpetvāna ~e … antepuraṃ pavesayi; Cp-a 135,.29 : ~ehi gaṇhāpetvā ~e vā attano rājapurise āṇāpetvā taṃ paribbājikaṃ gaṇhāpetvā); Mil 222,.28 (dāsidāsaceṭakaparivāraka-manussā); Ps V 46,.14 (rajjaṃ pahāya antamaso mukha-dhovanadāyakaṃ pi ~aṃ agahetvā); Mhv 33:37 (eko brāhmaṇaceṭako).

2ceṭaka
m. [cf AMg ceḍaya], a class of sāmaṇera; Sp 253,.35 (kumārako ti maṃ dhārehi cellako ~o moḷigallo samaṇuddeso ti maṃ dhārehī ti evaṃ sāmaṇeravevacanena sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ hoti, Be so; Ce, Ee monigallo; Se ~o peṭako moṇigallo; Sp-ṭ [Be] II 80,.2 : kumārako ti kumārāvattho ativiya daharasāmaṇero, cellako ti tato mahantataro khuddakasāmaṇero, ~o ti majjhimo, moḷigallo ti mahāsāmaṇero; ≠ Vmv [Be] I 135,.20 ≠ Vjb [Be] 99,.19).
coḷaka:
1coḷaka, colaka
n. [cf S. colaka, BHS coḍaka], a piece of cloth, a rag; Vin I 48,.9 (sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, ~aṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā); II 118,.15 (anujānāmi bhikkhave parissāvanan ti, ~aṃ na ppahoti); 150,.13 (~aṃ uppannaṃ hoti, anujānāmi bhikkhave cilimikaṃ kātun ti); 208,.17 (upāhānā puñchantena paṭhamaṃ sukkhena ~ena puñchitabbā pacchā allena); Pv 13:7 (bhikkhūnaṃ ālopaṃ datvā pāṇimattaṃ ca ~aṃ; Pv-a 70,.20 foll. : ekahattha-ppamāṇaṃ coḷakhaṇḍan ti attho); Mil 53,.33 (yato … araṇi siyā araṇipotako siyā araṇiyottakaṃ siyā uttarāraṇi siyā ~aṃ siyā purisassa ca tajjo vāyāmo siyā jāyeyya so aggī ti); Ps I 266,.32 (~āni pi kesañci saṇhāni kesañci thūlāni pāpuṇanti); Spk II 297,s (so paṃsukūlatthāya Sāvatthiṃ pavisitvā ~aṃ pariyesanto vicari); — ifc see āṇi-.

2coḷaka
mf (-ikā) n.,     colaka,    coḷika,   mfn., [cf S. cola, colakā], belonging to the Cola country; Sp 1212,.6 (hatthisoṇḍikaṃ nāma nābhimūlato hatthisoṇḍa-saṇṭhānaṃ olambakaṃ katvā nivatthaṃ coḷika-itthīnaṃ nivāsanaṃ viya, Be so; Ee colaka-itthīnaṃ; Se coḷaka-itthīnaṃ; Ce colakitthinivāsanaṃ) = Kkh2 252,.23 (Be, Ee so; Ce colikitthīnaṃ); Mhv 36:112 (bhikkhu coḷiko).
titta:
1titta
mfn. and m. [S. tikta], bitter; a bitter taste, bitterness; Abh 148; Sv 432,.20 (madhurato madhurarasaṃ yeva ~ato °-rasaṃ yeva phalaṃ hoti); —      °-alābu,   m.f., the bitter bottle-gourd; Sv 801,.15 = Vibh-a 113,.26; Vibh-a 113,.23 (~-valliṃ disvā, Be, Ee so; Ce tittakālābuvalliṃ; Se tittaṃ alābuvalliṃ disvā); —       °-kappa,   m., like bitterness; pure bitterness;? Nidd II 129,.16 (yathā atiloṇaṃ vuccati loṇakappo atitittakaṃ vuccati ~o … ati-uṇhaṃ vuccati aggikappo …, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se tittikappo) = Ap-a 133,.35 (Be, Se so; Ee atitittaṃ; Ce atittaṃ vuccati tittakakappo); —      atititta,   mfn., very bitter, too bitter; Pj II 59,.4 (nāccuṇhaṃ kiñci ajjhoharituṃ labhati nātisītaṃ … nātikaṭukaṃ nātitittaṃ, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se nātitittakaṃ).
udda:
1udda
m. [S. udra], a fish-eating animal; an otter; Ja III 51,.26 (tayo sahāyā ahesuṃ makkaṭo sigālo ~o ti); 335,28* (jīnā ~ā vivādena); Dhp-a III 141,.3 (dve ~ā mahantaṃ rohitamacchaṃ labhitvā); —      °-pota,   m., a young otter; Cp 1:10:2 (makkaṭo ca sigālo ca ~o c’ ahaṃ tadā, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se suttapoto; Cp-a 102,.28 : ~o cā ti ~o ca, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se suttapoto cā ti ~o ca); Cp-a 103,.30 (~o pāto va gocaraṃ pariyesissāmī ti nadītīraṃ gato).

2udda
n. [cf S. anudra, udrin], water; D II 14,.25 (yadā bodhisatto mātu kucchismā nikkhamati visado va nikkhamati amakkhito ~ena amakkhito semhena …; Sv 438,.1 : ~enā ti udakena; Sv-pṭ II 36,.20 : gabbhāsayagatena udakena) = M III 122,.34.
abhejjanaka:
abhejjanaka
mfn. [a3 + *bhejjana (from caus. pass. of bhindati) + ka2, or = abhijjanaka qv], indestructible; Ja I 393,1´ (nāpi ṭhitaṃ ~aṃ nāma atthi, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se abhijjanakaṃ); Cp-a 310,.25 (saddhammesu ca °-saddho).
abhippavassati:
abhippavassati

(pass.) rained upon; S III 155,.8 (bandhanāni … meghena ~āni, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee abhippavaṭṭāni) = V 51,.9 = A IV 127,18 ( Be, Ee, Se so; Ce abhippavaṭṭāni); Th-a III 140,.8 (mahāmeghena ~ā, Be, Se so; Ce atippavuṭṭhā; Ee atippavaṭṭā);  (b) abhippavaṭṭa,   abhippavaṭṭha,   mfn., 1. (act.) having rained; D II 343,.20 (mahāmegho ~o, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se abhippavuṭṭho); Ps I 98,.14 (mahāmegho abhippavaṭṭho, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se abhivuṭṭho); — 2. (pass.) rained upon; M I 306,.16 (meghena ~aṃ, Ee so; Be abhippavuṭṭhaṃ; Ce abhippavaṭṭhaṃ; Se abhivuṭṭhaṃ).
abhisamaya:
abhisamaya
m. [BHS id.], 1. penetration into; right understanding (of); D II 31,.8 (Vipassissa bodhisattassa yonisomanasikārā ahu paññāya ~o); A IV 384,.20 (yaṃ … aññātaṃ … anabhisametaṃ, tassa ñāṇāya dassanāya pattiyā sacchikiriyāya ~āya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī ti); Th 593 (saccānaṃ ~o); Paṭis II 215,.3 foll. (Paṭis-a 686,.19 : ~o ti saccānaṃ abhimukhena samāgamo, paṭivedho ti attho); Mil 289,.22 (catunnaṃ yeva ariyasaccānaṃ ~aṃ anvesi); Peṭ 125,.14 (catūsu ariyasaccesu yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ ~o); 133,.17 (cattāro ~ā); Sadd 899,.29 (aññatra buddhuppādā ~o n’ atthi); — ifc see dhammâ-, mānâ-, saccâ-; — 2. convincement, conversion; Bv 15:3 (tassāpi lokanāthassa ahesuṃ ~ā tayo koṭisatasahassānaṃ paṭhamābhisamayo ahu); Sv 549,.33 (aññesu ca ṭhānesu anekā ~ā dissanti); Bv-a 129,.1 foll. (tato ~o na bhaveyya asati ~e niratthako buddhappādo bhaveyya); —     anabhisamaya,   m., lack of penetration; wrong understanding; S III 260,.23 (rūpe … ~ā); Dhs 390 (aññānaṃ adassanaṃ ~o ananubodho … moho hoti) ≠ Nett 75,.26; Peṭ 119,.18 (catūsu ariyasaccesu ~o).
abhivuḍḍhikāma:
abhivuḍḍhi, abhivuddhi
f. [S. abhivṛddhi], growth, increase; prosperity; Vv-a 39,.25 (attano ~iṃ patthayamānena); Mhv 5:195 (sāsanassābhivuddhiṃ ca taṃhetukaṃ avekkhiya); 81:64; —      °-kāma,   mfn., wishing for the growth or prosperity; Vism 321,.11 (daharassa ~ā) = As 196,.3; —       °-kāraṇa,   n. [abhivuḍḍhi + kāraṇa1], a cause of growth or prosperity; Cp-a 35,.18 (maṅgalaṃ ~an ti abhisammataṃ); — see also abhivaḍḍhi.
accokkaṭṭha:
accokkaṭṭha
mfn. [ati + pp of *o2 + kasati3, kassati1, cf S. avakṛṣṭa; -kk- by analogy with accukkaṭṭha qv], (of a robe) pulled down too far; M II 139,.21 (na ca tassa bhoto Gotamassa kāye cīvaraṃ accukkaṭṭhaṃ hoti na ca ~aṃ; Ps III 393,.12 foll. : yo yāva gopphakā otāretvā va pārupati tassa ~aṃ hoti … yo ekaṃsaṃ katvā thanaṃ vivaritvā yāti tassa pi ~aṃ).
adhicittaṃ:
adhicittaṃ
ind. [adhi + acc. of citta1; taken by cts as acc. of adhicitta; cf Sadd 748,.2 foll.], as regards thought; as to meditation; Vin III 235,.3 (bhikkhuniyo … riñcanti uddesaṃ paripucchaṃ adhisīlaṃ ~aṃ adhipaññaṃ); A I 236,8* (adhisīlaṃ ~aṃ ca adhipaññaṃ ca viriyavā); 240,.17 (bhikkhuno adhisīlaṃ pi sikkhato ~aṃ pi sikkhato adhipaññaṃ pi sikkhato); 254,.11 (santi ~aṃ anuyuttassa bhikkhuno oḷārikā upakkilesā; cf Mp II 362,.12 : ~an ti samathavipassanācittaṃ); Nidd I 149,.5 (adhisīlaṃ pi sikkheyya ~aṃ pi sikkheyya adhipaññaṃ pi sikkheyya); Paṭis I 167,.17 (samathanimittupaṭṭhānekattaṃ ca ~aṃ anuyuttānaṃ; cf Paṭis-a 543,.12 foll. : vipassanāya pādakabhāvena adhicittasaṅkhātaṃ samādhiṃ anuyuttānaṃ, Be, Se so).
adhigacchati:
adhigacchati
pr. 3 sg. [S. adhigacchati], gets to; attains, acquires; finds; understands; Vin I 228,.2 (mahantaṃ bhogakkhandhaṃ ~ati); D I 224,.11 (samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ ~eyya); M I 275,.15 (~e somanassaṃ); S I 154,.18 (sa ce ratiṃ nādhigaccheyya tattha, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr nādhigacchaye) = Th 142; A I 162,29* (anupubbena nibbānaṃ ~anti paṇḍitā); Dhp 187 (api dibbesu kāmesu ratiṃ so nādhigacchati); It 82,8* (santim evādhigacchati); Thī 51 (attānaṃ ~a Ubbiri); Ja V 266,28* (nirayā nādhigacchanti dvāraṃ nikkhamanesino); Pv 7:4 (nibbutiṃ nādhigacchāmi); Ap 25,.25 (tuvaṃ pi ~ehi gacchāma buddhasantikaṃ, Ee, Se so; Be tvaṃ pi taṃ adhigacchesi; Ce tvaṃ pi taṃ ~āhi); — adhigacchati in Ee at Sv 921,.15 is wr for adhibhavati (Be, Ce, Se so); — fut. 3 sg. adhigamissati, M I 247,.12 (yaṃ no samaṇo Gotamo dhammaṃ adhigamissati taṃ no ārocessatī ti); 1 sg. (a) adhigamissāmi, Nidd II (Be) 228,.7 (cf Ee 131,.16); (b) adhigacchissāmi, Nidd I 67,.21 (~issāmi phusayissāmi); 3 pl. (a) adhigamissanti, Paṭis II 55,.23 (nekkhammaṃ … adhigatā vā ~anti vā adhigamissanti vā); (b) adhigacchissanti, Ps II 117,.24 (anvesantā pi kiṃ ~issanti); — part.pr. adhigacchanta, mf (~antī) n., It-a I 92,.23 (~antassa); Thī-a 249,.15 (mayā … ~antiyā); — neg. anadhigacchanta, mfn., Ja I 113,27´; Nidd I 440,.9; — aor 3 sg. (a) ajjhagamā, D III 170,2*; Sn 5 (yo nājjhagamā bhavesu sāraṃ); Ja III 450,22* (Udayo ajjhagamā mahattapattaṃ); — for ajjhagamā in eds at Vin III 147,22* = Ja II 285,23* and at Sn 379 read jagāma qv sv gacchati; (b) ajjhagacchi, ajjhagañchi, Ja V 255,19* (dīpaṃ so na ajjhagacchi agati yattha pakkhinaṃ, Ee so; Ce, Se ajjhagañchi; Be najjhagāgañchi; 256,23´ foll. attano patiṭṭhānaṃ na ajjhagacchī ti adhigañchī ti attho, Ee so; Ce na ajjhagañchi nādhigañchī ti; Se nādhigacchī ti; Be na ajjhagā nāgañchī ti); VI 202,23* (Ce, Ee ajjhagañchi; Be, Se ajjhagacchi); (c) adhigacchi, adhigañchi, D II 352,.1 (adhigacchi); Ja V 256,24´ (adhigañchī ti, Ee so; Ce nādhigañchī ti; Se nādhigacchī ti; Be nāgañchī ti); Ap-a 133,.3; — 2 sg. (a) ajjhagamā, M I 172,.9 (tvaṃ … nājjhagamā); (b) ajjhagamāsi, Ja V 171,8* (pucchāmi te nāgarāja tam atthaṃ kath’ ajjhagamāsi vimānaseṭṭhaṃ); — 1 sg. (a) ajjhagamaṃ, A I 259,.14 (yo loke assādo tad ajjhagamaṃ); Ap 49,.9 (bodhiṃ ajjhagamaṃ ahaṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ajjhāgamaṃ); (b) ajjhagamiṃ, Th 117 (tisso vijjā ajjhagamiṃ); (c) adhigamiṃ, Pj II 393,.9; (d) adhigacchiṃ, D II 341,.19; Thī 221 (amataṃ ~iṃ); (e) adhigacchissaṃ, Sn 446 (satta vassāni bhagavantaṃ anubandhiṃ … otāraṃ nādhigacchissaṃ sambuddhassa satīmato; Pj II 393,.9 : nādhigacchissan ti nādhigamiṃ); — 3 pl. (a) ajjhagamaṃsu, M I 173,.11; (b) ajjhagamuṃ, S I 12,13* (pariyesamānā nājjhagamuṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee nājjhāgamuṃ; perhaps read na ca ājagāmuṃ qv sv āgacchati); 22,7* (nibbānam ev’ ajjhagamuṃ sapaññā) = Ja III 473,2* (Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ajjhagamū); (c) ajjhagaṃsu, Ja II 296,11* (Ce, Ee so; Se ajjhaggaṃsu; Be ajjhagamuṃ); (d) adhigamiṃsu, Pj I 194,.11; (e) adhigacchiṃsu, Ja I 256,12´; — 1 pl. ajjhagamāmase, Ja VI 442,12*; —     part.perf.act.     adhigatava(t),   mfn., who has attained; Vv-a 296,.13 (nibbānam eva vā upagate, ~ante ti attho); — absol. (a) adhigamma, A IV 447,.30 (saññāvedayitanirodhe ānisaṃsaṃ adhigamma); Th 1106; Ja III 523,15* (yo sāhasena adhigamma bhoge); — neg. anadhigamma, Pj II 67,.23; — (b) adhigantvā, D I 224,.12 (kusalaṃ dhammaṃ adhigantvā); Ja I 45,.11; Ap 342,.17; Mil 380,.16; — neg. anadhigantvā, It-a II 99,.32; Thī-a 43,.1; —      pass. 3 sg. (a)    adhigamī̆yati,   Vism 440,.32 (~īyati saṃpāpuṇīyati) ≠ Nidd-a I 340,.19 = Paṭis-a 3,.23 (Be so; Ce, Ee, Se adhigammati);  (b)   adhigammati,   Paṭis-a 3,.23 (~ati, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be adhigamīyati); —      pp     adhigata,   mfn. and n. [ts], 1. (mfn.) (i) (pass.) attained; found; understood; Vin I 4,.33 (~o kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro); D II 34,.34 (~o … vipassanāmaggo); Thī 513 (~aṃ idaṃ bahūhi amataṃ); Ja III 329,20* (dhanaṃ ca me ~aṃ); — neg. anadhigata, mfn., 1. not attained, what has not been attained; Vin III 91,.6 (anadhigate adhigatasaññino); Vibh 385,.24 (anadhigatassa adhigamāya); — (ii) (act.) having reached; who has attained or understood; Paṭis II 55,.23 (ye hi keci nekkhammaṃ … ~ā vā adhigacchanti vā); Ja V 326,27* (adhigat’ amhā tame ñāṇaṃ, Ce, Se so; Ee amha; Be adhigamā; 327,2´ : mayam … ñāṇaṃ adhigatā); Kv 302,.2 (arahattaṃ pattassa paṭiladdhassa ~assa); Dhp-a III 129,.5 (arahattaṃ ~o ’smī ti); — neg. anadhigata, mfn., who has not attained; Kv 257,.11 (atthi koci adibbacakkhuko dibbacakkhuṃ appaṭiladdho anadhigato asacchikato); Vism 699,.25 (anadhigatattā); — 2. aggappasāda:

m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
